tldr: Headlines across all 16 buckets frame Trump's Russian diesel deal through four overlapping lenses: a midterm-election gambit, a supply fix for record pump prices, a security concession that Ukraine warns funds Russia's war, and a formal reversal of US sanctions policy — with roughly two-thirds of outlets foregrounding the political or economic rationale while Zelensky's 'investment in war' warning appears as a secondary clause rather than the lede.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to make Zelensky's refinery-strike defiance the headline cause of the deal — 'Trump pressured Ukraine to unilaterally halt strikes on Russian oil refineries' — framing Trump's action as reactive punishment of Ukraine rather than as proactive deal-making with Russia.

Only headline to use 'U-Turn' language ('In A U-Turn, Trump Signs Oil Deal With Putin'), treating the sanctions reversal as a policy inconsistency rather than as a diplomatic achievement — the lone headline that foregrounds the contradiction with Trump's own recent sanctions legislation.

Only headline to explicitly attribute the deal's origin to Zelensky's non-compliance — 'Trump cut deal with Putin after Zelensky ignored his requests' — sourcing the causal chain to a named US official and inverting the standard narrative of Trump pursuing Russia.

Only headline to use direct Ukrainian voice as the entire headline event — ''We're being used as a front,' Zelensky says' — making Ukraine the subject of manipulation rather than reporting the deal as the primary fact, a framing absent from all other 35 outlets.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents the Trump-Putin diesel deal predominantly as an economic and political event — record prices, midterms — while the security betrayal frame (war funding, Zelensky's fury) surfaces strongly only in Ukraine-adjacent and pan-Arab outlets, leaving the formal sanctions reversal as a sub-headline detail in most Western coverage.
